examples.ko: 이번 휴가는 최장 열흘까지 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take up to ten days off this time.
This tunnel is the longest in our country.

examples.ko: 비는 최장 사흘 동안 올 거예요.
examples.en: The rain will last three days at most.
Who set the longest record?
I heard the holiday can be as long as nine days.

examples.ko: 최장 거리를 걸은 사람에게 상을 줬어요.
examples.en: They gave a prize to the person who walked the farthest.

explain: '가장 긴'이라는 뜻이지만 '최장 열흘'처럼 숫자 앞에서 '길어야 이만큼'이라는 상한선을 말할 때 특히 많이 써요. 반대로 '가장 짧은'은 '최단'이에요. 시간, 거리, 기간에 쓰고 사람 키에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The maximum length of the visa is three months.
phrases.nuance_ko: 허용되는 가장 긴 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the longest period that is allowed.

phrases.example: 이 표는 최장 일 년까지 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can use this ticket for up to one year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자 뒤에 '까지'를 붙여서 '길어도 이만큼'이라는 뜻을 만들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '까지' after a number gives the sense 'at the very most this long'.

phrases.en: This rainy season is the longest on record.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 '지금까지 중 가장 길다'고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news to say 'longest ever'.

explain_en: It means the longest, but it is most often placed before a number, as in 최장 열흘, to set an upper limit: at most ten days. The opposite is 최단 (the shortest). It is used for time, distance, and duration, not for a person's height.

examples.en: This movie is a modern version of the story of Sim Cheong.
These days the internet is a modern-day library.
A modern Cinderella story came out as a drama.
His friends call him a modern-day Hong Gildong.
They remade the old tale as a modern version.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 현대판 장터 같은 분위기예요.
examples.en: This shop has the feel of a modern-day market.

explain: '현대판 + 명사'나 '~의 현대판'처럼 쓰고, 옛이야기·인물·제도를 오늘날에 맞게 바꾼 것을 말해요. '현대판 홍길동'처럼 비유로 많이 써요. 원래 이야기는 '원작'이나 '고전'이라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 가난한 사람을 돕는 현대판 홍길동이에요.
phrases.en: He is a modern-day Hong Gildong who helps poor people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛 인물을 오늘날의 사람에 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare a person today to a figure from old stories.

phrases.en: This drama is a modern Cinderella story.
phrases.nuance_ko: '현대판' 뒤에 이야기 속 인물이나 제목을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a story character or title after 현대판.

phrases.en: This comic is a modern version of Heungbu and Nolbu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'A의 현대판'으로 원래 이야기를 오늘날에 맞게 바꾼 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the pattern 'A의 현대판', it means an old story adapted to today.

explain_en: It is used as '현대판 + noun' or '~의 현대판' for an old story, figure or system adapted to today. It is often figurative, as in '현대판 홍길동'. The original is called '원작' or '고전'.

en: to be foul-smelling; to be stinking

examples.ko: 창고 문을 열자 고리타분한 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: When I opened the storeroom door, there was a musty smell.
The old blanket gives off a stale smell.
My father's way of thinking is a bit old-fashioned.
Please stop with that stuffy old talk.
It's damp inside the closet, so it smells stale.

examples.ko: 규칙이 너무 고리타분해서 아무도 안 좋아해요.
examples.en: The rules are so outdated and stuffy that nobody likes them.

explain: 냄새가 퀴퀴할 때도 쓰지만, 생각이나 방식이 낡고 답답할 때 더 많이 써요. '구식이다'나 '케케묵다'와 비슷해요. 상대방에게 직접 말하면 무례하게 들려요.

phrases.en: The old book gives off a musty smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래되어 퀴퀴한 냄새를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a stale, musty smell from age.

phrases.example: 아버지는 고리타분한 생각을 바꾸고 싶어 하세요.
phrases.en: My father wants to change his old-fashioned way of thinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낡고 답답한 생각을 말하며, 다른 사람에게 쓰면 무례할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means stuffy old ideas; can be rude if aimed at someone.

phrases.en: The story of this movie is too stale.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 낡고 재미없는 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite form for something that feels outdated and dull.

explain_en: It can describe a stale smell, but it is more often used for thinking or methods that feel outdated and stuffy. It is close to '구식이다' and '케케묵다'. Saying it directly to someone sounds rude.

examples.en: My grandfather is really stubborn.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 고집불통이라서 말이 안 통해요.
examples.en: He's so hardheaded that you can't reason with him.
It's not easy to persuade my stubborn younger sibling.

examples.ko: 남편이 고집불통이라 매번 제가 져 줘요.
examples.en: My husband is so stubborn that I always give in.
Working under a stubborn boss is hard.
If you act so stubborn, you'll lose your friends.

explain: 사람을 흉볼 때 쓰는 말이라서 대부분 좋지 않은 느낌이에요. '고집쟁이'보다 훨씬 세서 아예 말이 안 통한다는 느낌이 있어요. '고집이 세다'는 조금 더 부드러운 표현이에요.

phrases.en: It's hard to talk with a headstrong person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인'을 붙이면 사람을 꾸며 줄 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-인' lets it describe a person.

phrases.example: 제 동생은 고집이 세서 잘 안 바뀌어요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling is stubborn and doesn't change easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고집불통'보다 부드러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a softer expression than '고집불통'.

phrases.example: 아버지는 한번 정하면 끝까지 하는 고집불통이에요.
phrases.en: My father is stubborn and sticks to whatever he decides.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 쓰면 그 사람의 성격을 한마디로 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a predicate, it sums up a person's character in one word.

explain_en: This is used to criticize a person, so it usually sounds negative. It is much stronger than '고집쟁이', suggesting someone you simply can't reason with. '고집이 세다' is a softer way to say it.

examples.en: My father's cell phone is totally outdated.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 생각이 구닥다리라서 말이 안 통해요.
examples.en: His thinking is so old-fashioned that we can't communicate.
It's an ancient computer, so the programs are very slow.
I was a bit upset to be treated as old-fashioned.

examples.ko: 구닥다리인 줄 알았는데 써 보니 쓸 만해요.
examples.en: I thought it was outdated, but it turns out to be quite usable.
Please don't see me as old-fashioned.

explain: 물건, 생각, 사람에게 다 쓸 수 있어요. 중립적인 '구식'보다 낮추는 느낌이 강해서, 친한 사이에서 농담처럼 쓰거나 윗사람에게는 조심하는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: This computer is old-fashioned, so it is slow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '구닥다리'와 뜻은 비슷하지만 낮추는 느낌이 없어서 누구에게나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to 구닥다리 but without the put-down feel, so anyone can use it.

phrases.en: This song feels a bit outdated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '같다'를 붙여서 구식이라는 느낌이 든다고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 같다 softly says it feels outdated.

phrases.en: Please don't tease me about having an outdated idea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘과 맞지 않는 옛날 생각을 말할 때 써요. 농담처럼 쓰는 경우도 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for old-fashioned ideas that don't fit these days, often jokingly.

explain_en: It can be used for objects, ideas and people. It sounds more belittling than the neutral '구식', so it fits jokes among close friends, and you should be careful using it about someone older.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 성격 차이가 극명히 드러났어요.
examples.en: The difference in the two people's personalities became strikingly clear.

examples.ko: 이 사진이 그날의 상황을 극명히 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This photo shows the situation that day very clearly.
The results were so starkly different that everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 이 실험은 그 차이를 극명히 증명했어요.
examples.en: This experiment proved that difference unmistakably.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 생활 모습이 극명히 대비돼요.
examples.en: The way of life in the two countries contrasts sharply.

examples.ko: 점수가 극명히 갈린 걸 보면 준비 차이가 컸어요.
examples.en: Seeing how sharply the scores split, the difference in preparation was big.

explain: 차이나 모습이 아주 뚜렷하게 보일 때 써요. 주로 '드러나다', '보여 주다', '대비되다', '갈리다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요. 말할 때는 '극명하게'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 두 팀의 실력 차이가 극명하게 보였어요.
phrases.en: The difference in skill between the two teams was starkly clear.
phrases.nuance_ko: '극명히'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때는 '극명하게'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 극명히; 극명하게 sounds more natural in speech.

phrases.example: 두 도시는 생활 모습에서 극명한 차이를 보여요.
phrases.en: The two cities show a stark difference in way of life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '극명하다'를 명사 앞에 써서 아주 뚜렷한 차이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective 극명하다 before a noun describes a very clear difference.

phrases.example: 밝은 색과 어두운 색이 극명히 대비돼요.
phrases.en: Bright and dark colors contrast sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지가 서로 아주 다르게 보일 때 '대비되다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 대비되다 when two things look very different from each other.

explain_en: It is used when a difference or appearance is very clear. It mostly appears with words like '드러나다' (be revealed), '보여 주다' (show), '대비되다' (contrast) and '갈리다' (split). In speech people also say '극명하게'.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 근대식으로 지어져서 분위기가 독특해요.
examples.en: This building was built in a modern-era style, so it has a unique atmosphere.
My grandfather is from the generation that received modern-style education.

examples.ko: 근대식 병원이 처음 생긴 때를 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned when the first modern-style hospital appeared.

examples.ko: 거리에 근대식 건물이 아직 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Some modern-era buildings still remain on the street.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 근대식 교실을 그대로 보존했어요.
examples.en: That school preserved its modern-era classroom as it was.

examples.ko: 근대식 설비를 들여와 공장을 새로 지었어요.
examples.en: They brought in modern equipment and built the factory anew.

explain: '전통식'과 반대로, 개화기 이후 서양에서 들어온 방식이나 모양을 말해요. 보통 '근대식 건물', '근대식 교육'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. '현대식'은 지금 쓰는 최신 방식이라 시기가 달라요.

phrases.example: 서울에는 근대식 건물이 아직 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: There are still modern-era style buildings in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근대식'은 보통 이렇게 명사 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 근대식 is usually placed before a noun like this.

phrases.example: 그 학교는 100년 전에 세운 근대식 학교예요.
phrases.en: That school is a modern-era style school built 100 years ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전 서당과 달리 새로 들어온 방식으로 가르치는 학교를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a school using newly introduced methods, unlike the old village schools.

phrases.example: 전통식 집과 근대식 집을 같이 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can see both traditional-style and modern-era style houses.
phrases.nuance_ko: '근대식'과 반대로 옛날부터 내려온 방식을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 근대식; it refers to ways passed down from long ago.

explain_en: In contrast to '전통식' (traditional style), it refers to methods or looks that came from the West after the opening of the country. It is usually placed before a noun, as in '근대식 건물' and '근대식 교육'. '현대식' means today's up-to-date style, so the era is different.

examples.en: My hands are so rough.
I haven't slept for days, so my skin is rough and dull.
I wiped my face with a scratchy towel.
I didn't shave, so my chin got stubbly.
In winter my lips get rough, so I put on balm.
The surface of this paper is rough.

explain: '꺼칠하다'를 반복해서 거칠고 마른 느낌을 더 강조한 말이에요. 피부, 입술, 머리카락, 수염처럼 만졌을 때 매끄럽지 않은 것에 많이 써요. 반대로 매끄럽고 부드러우면 '부드럽다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I shaved my rough stubble in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'으로 명사를 꾸며서 만졌을 때 거친 것을 말해요. 수염과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form describes something rough to the touch. It suits stubble well.

phrases.example: 잠을 못 자서 얼굴이 꺼칠꺼칠해 보여요.
phrases.en: Your face looks rough because you haven't slept.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아 보이다'를 붙여 겉모습을 말해요. 피곤해 보일 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아 보이다' it describes appearance, often when someone looks tired.

phrases.en: My skin was rough, so I put on moisturizer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄인 말이에요. '꺼칠꺼칠하다'보다 조금 덜 강조하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shorter form. It feels slightly less emphatic than '꺼칠꺼칠하다'.

explain_en: It repeats '꺼칠하다' to stress a rough, dry feel. It is common for skin, lips, hair and stubble, things that feel not smooth to the touch. The opposite is '부드럽다' (soft, smooth).

examples.ko: 선생님은 늘 나긋나긋한 목소리로 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: The teacher always explains in a soft, gentle voice.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말투가 나긋나긋해서 듣기 편해요.
examples.en: That person's way of speaking is gentle, so it's easy to listen to.

examples.ko: 화가 났는데도 나긋나긋하게 말해서 더 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Even though she was angry, she spoke so softly that it was even scarier.

examples.ko: 나긋나긋하지만 할 말은 다 하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: She is gentle but says everything she needs to say.

examples.ko: 처음 만났을 때 그 사람은 아주 나긋나긋했어요.
examples.en: When we first met, that person was very gentle.
Just because someone is soft-spoken doesn't mean they are weak.

explain: 주로 말투, 목소리, 태도가 부드럽고 상냥할 때 써요. 반대로 무뚝뚝하고 거칠게 말하는 모습에는 '퉁명스럽다'를 써요. 칭찬으로 쓰이는 일이 많지만, 겉으로만 부드러운 사람을 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.example: 안내원이 나긋나긋한 목소리로 길을 알려 줬어요.
phrases.en: The guide gave directions in a soft voice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 쓰는 형태로, 목소리와 가장 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form, which pairs best with 'voice'.

phrases.en: My older sister is always gentle when she speaks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 말투나 태도를 말하는 해요체 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite conjugation used to describe someone's way of speaking or manner.

phrases.en: Please speak softly to the baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부드럽고 상냥하게 말하는 방식을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes speaking in a gentle, kind way.

explain_en: It is mainly used when someone's way of speaking, voice or attitude is soft and kind. The opposite, curt and rough speech, is '퉁명스럽다'. It is often a compliment, but it can also describe someone who is only gentle on the surface.

examples.ko: 저는 내향성이 강해서 사람 많은 곳이 피곤해요.
examples.en: I'm quite introverted, so crowded places tire me out.

examples.ko: 내향성인 사람도 발표를 잘할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Introverted people can give good presentations too.

examples.ko: 내향성과 외향성 중에서 나는 어디에 가까울까요?
examples.en: Between introversion and extroversion, which am I closer to?

examples.ko: 친구는 내향성 성격이라 조용한 카페를 좋아해요.
examples.en: My friend has an introverted personality, so she likes quiet cafés.
Introversion is not a flaw but just one type of personality.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 내향성 때문에 낯선 모임을 힘들어해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling finds unfamiliar gatherings hard because of introversion.

explain: 반대말은 '외향성'이에요. 사람을 직접 말할 때는 '내향적이다', '내향적인 사람'이 더 자연스럽고, '내향성'은 성격 특성을 설명할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 내향성이 강한 사람은 혼자 쉬는 시간이 필요해요.
phrases.en: People with strong introversion need time to rest alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격의 정도를 설명할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for describing how introverted someone is.

phrases.en: I'm a little introverted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 직접 말할 때는 '내향성'보다 이 말이 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: When describing a person directly, this is more natural than 'naehyangseong'.

phrases.en: Introverted people like quiet places.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격을 가진 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to a person with this personality.

explain_en: The opposite is '외향성' (extroversion). When describing a person directly, '내향적이다' or '내향적인 사람' sounds more natural, while '내향성' is used to talk about the trait itself.

examples.en: The bread has baked to a light golden yellow.
Now that it's autumn, the ginkgo leaves are turning yellowish.
The yellowish curry looks delicious.
Fry the egg until it turns a light golden color.
The wallpaper turned yellowish in the sunlight.
I spread soft, pale yellow butter on the bread.

explain: '노랗다'보다 색이 옅고 부드러운 노란빛을 말해요. 빵이나 전처럼 구워진 것, 낙엽이나 종이처럼 색이 변한 것에 잘 어울려요. 구워진 모습은 '노릇노릇'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The paper of the old book is yellowish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래되어 색이 옅게 변한 물건에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suits old things whose color has faded to a pale yellow.

phrases.en: After leaving it for a long time, the photo turned yellowish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 점점 옅은 노란빛으로 변하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes color gradually turning pale yellow.

phrases.en: Pan-fry the pancake until it is golden brown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구워진 음식의 보기 좋은 색을 말할 때 '노르스름하다' 대신 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used instead of 노르스름하다 for the pleasing color of cooked food.

explain_en: It describes a paler, softer yellow than '노랗다'. It suits things that are baked, such as bread or jeon, and things whose color has changed, like fallen leaves or paper. The look of well-baked food can also be called '노릇노릇'.

examples.en: The old paper has turned a dingy yellow.

examples.ko: 형광등 불빛 아래라서 얼굴이 누리끼리해 보여요.
examples.en: Under the fluorescent light, your face looks sallow.
The white shirt has turned yellowish after wearing it for so long.
I want to make my yellowed teeth white.
The wallpaper has yellowed, so we decided to replace it.

examples.ko: 오래된 책은 종이가 누리끼리하고 냄새도 나요.
examples.en: Old books have yellowed pages and a musty smell.

explain: '노랗다'가 산뜻한 노란색이라면 이 말은 탁하고 칙칙한 누런색이에요. 오래된 종이, 낡은 옷, 안 좋은 안색처럼 별로 좋지 않은 느낌으로 써요. '누렇다', '누르스름하다'와 비슷해요.

phrases.en: The wallpaper is old, so it turned a dull yellow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탁한 누런색을 말할 때 쓰는 꾸미는 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifying form for a dull, dirty yellow color.

phrases.en: My white clothes turned yellowish after I wore them for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'를 붙여서 색이 변했다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어지다' shows that the color has changed.

phrases.en: The pickled radish is yellowish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누리끼리하다와 비슷하지만 덜 칙칙하고 연한 누런색이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 누리끼리하다 but a lighter, less dingy yellow.

explain_en: While '노랗다' is a bright, clean yellow, this word is a dull, murky yellow. It is used with a negative feel, for old paper, worn clothes or an unhealthy complexion. It is similar to '누렇다' and '누르스름하다'.

examples.en: Everyone was surprised by that child's boldness.
This job needs a little boldness.

examples.ko: 신인 감독의 대담성이 영화 곳곳에서 느껴져요.
examples.en: The new director's boldness can be felt throughout the film.
He has boldness, but he is quite unprepared.
The interviewers thought highly of his boldness.

examples.ko: 그는 대담성과 신중함을 모두 갖춘 사람이에요.
examples.en: He is a person who has both boldness and caution.

explain: '대담하다'의 성질을 말할 때 쓰고 '대담성이 있다/없다/부족하다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '배짱', '용기'가 있고 반대되는 말은 '소심함'이에요. 칭찬할 때도 쓰지만 '무모함'에 가까운 뜻으로 말할 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: That person is bold in both words and actions.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대담성'의 형용사 형태로, 사람이나 행동을 직접 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form of 대담성, used to describe a person or action directly.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 배짱이 있어서 발표를 잘해요.
phrases.en: That friend has guts, so they give good presentations.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대담성'보다 구어체이고 겁 없는 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More colloquial than 대담성, referring to a fearless attitude.

phrases.example: 그 감독은 새로운 시도에서 대담성을 보였어요.
phrases.en: The director showed boldness in trying something new.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁 없이 해 낸 일을 평가할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for praising something done fearlessly.

explain_en: It names the quality of being '대담하다' (bold), as in '대담성이 있다/없다/부족하다'. Close words are '배짱' and '용기', and the opposite is '소심함'. It can be praise, but sometimes it leans toward recklessness.

examples.ko: 지금 두 나라는 서로 대립적 관계에 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries are now in an opposing relationship.

examples.ko: 대립적 입장을 가진 사람들이 오늘 처음 만났어요.
examples.en: People with opposing positions met for the first time today.

examples.ko: 이 둘을 대립적 개념으로만 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't see these two only as opposing concepts.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 선과 악의 대립적 구도로 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: The film is built on an opposing structure of good and evil.

examples.ko: 지금은 대립적 상황이라서 결론이 안 나요.
examples.en: It is a situation of opposition right now, so no conclusion is reached.

examples.ko: 무조건 대립적 시각으로만 보지 말고 함께 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Let's think together instead of always seeing it from an opposing view.

explain: '대립적 관계', '대립적 입장'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. 서술할 때는 '대립적이다'나 '대립적인'으로 말하기도 해요. 서로 맞서거나 반대되는 상태를 말하는 글이나 토론에서 많이 보여요.

phrases.en: The two people's opinions are opposed to each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술할 때 쓰는 형태로, 서로 반대되는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The predicate form, describing a state of being opposed.

phrases.en: The two teams are in an opposing relationship.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대립적인'은 명사 앞에서 관계나 입장을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 대립적인 modifies nouns like relationship or stance.

phrases.en: The two people's opinions clash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 서로 맞서는 행동이나 상태를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb, it expresses actively standing against each other.

explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '대립적 관계' or '대립적 입장'. You can also say '대립적이다' or '대립적인'. It appears often in writing and debates about things that oppose or contrast each other.
